title: feedback-mosaic-actionable-extracts-oct-2027
content:
Summary:
This is a synthesis of customer feedback collected from Sept 2027 field interviews, support transcripts, and a lightweight NPS follow-up survey. Goal: translate fragmented asks into a compact set of actionable feature requests and quick-win engineering tickets. This is a working doc — rough prioritization and recommended owners included but not finalized.

Methodology / signal sources:
- 12 customer interviews (product & platform leads at mid-market SaaS) recorded 2027-09-10 -> 2027-09-24.
- Aggregated 48 support threads flagged as "prod-impact" (helpdesk tags) between 2027-08-01 and 2027-09-30.
- Quick NPS follow-up (n=87) with an open-text "one improvement" question.
- One internal beta test summary from Partner X (private deployment) with performance logs attached (see linked JIRA CS-2012).

Top emergent themes (ranked by frequency & impact):
1) Predictable tail latency under bursty traffic (HIGH impact, common):
   - Customers report occasional 500-800ms extra tail for short-lived bursts — causes UX glitches in chat widgets and downstream user timeouts.
   - Repeated ask: visibility into request-level queueing + ability to set per-route latency SLOs (not just average).

2) Fallback model semantics and observability (MED-HIGH):
   - Several customers are using the routing fallback feature but want clearer labeling of fallback events in traces + automated summary of quality diffs between primary and fallback model for pay / billing reconciliation.
   - Proposal: add a "fallback diff report" per rollout window (sampled outputs + KL-like divergence score + token-cost delta).

3) Cost visibility at prompt/component level (MED):
   - Requests to show token and cost breakdown tied to function/tool-calling paths (e.g., cost for tool A vs model generation).
   - Want to be able to attribute customer invoices to developer routes or product features.

4) Simpler local emulation for Private deployments (MED):
   - Smaller customers pushing Private want a lightweight dev-mode for Local VPC testing (single-machine, CPU-quantized) to run safety checks before on-prem rollout.

5) Eval-driven regression alerts (LOW-MED but sticky):
   - Customers want auto-triggered alerts when model rollout causes statistically significant drift on their golden promptset. Some already maintain their own scripts; ask is for managed feature.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We saw a spike during our campaign launch and the chat started returning partial outputs — hard to debug because traces only show averages. We need to know which requests hit the slow path." — PM, adtech startup
- "Fallback is great but it silently changed hallucination rate and we weren't alerted. Billing didn't match perceived quality." — Infra lead, fintech
- "If we could run the same model locally in dev with a smaller backend, our SREs would catch issues before we push private. Right now on-prem tests are expensive." — Platform eng, healthcare

High-impact feature requests (recommended next workstreams):
A) Per-request queue/latency visibility + per-route SLOs (owner: eng-observability) 
   - What: Trace-level annotations for queue wait time + indicator for bodied/fast-path vs slow-path. UI: per-route histogram + percentile slider.
   - Customer benefit: reduces debug time, supports SLA contracts.
   - Rough effort: 3 sprints (backend tracing + small console change).
   - Quick win steps: add queue-time header to all responses (can be consumed by customers immediately).
   - Linked: JIRA CS-1897 (obs: queue-metrics)

B) Rollout fallback diff report (owner: product-hosted-api + applied-ml)
   - What: Sample paired outputs from primary + fallback during rollouts; auto-generate a short summary (fluency metrics, content divergence, token delta).
   - Customer benefit: clarity on quality tradeoffs and billing reconciliation.
   - Rough effort: 2-4 sprints + small UI.

C) Route-level cost attribution (owner: optimize + console)
   - What: map costs to routes and enable tagging of token usage by tool/function call.
   - Quick win: exportable CSV with route-level token counts per day.

D) Local dev-mode for Private (owner: private-deployments)
   - What: single-binary local runtime that emulates VPC networking and provides quantized model variants for smoke tests.
   - Why: reduces friction for on-prem adoption, lowers integration cost for smaller customers.

E) Built-in rollout regression alerts (owner: product-hosted-api + optimize)
   - What: allow customers to register golden prompts and get automatic alerts when rollout changes metric beyond threshold.

Quick wins (<= 2 weeks) that we can spin up as tickets:
- Add queue-time and kv-cache-hit headers to response (dev: infra-runtime) — owner: site-reliability-engineering, ETA: 10 business days.
- Console CSV export for per-route daily token counts (owner: console-team) — ETA: 7 business days.
- Beta doc + runbook for customers to label fallback events in existing traces (owner: customer-success) — ETA: 3 business days.

Risk flags / considerations:
- Adding per-request tracing could increase overhead on runtime; need perf benchmark and sampling strategy.
- Fallback diff sampling must respect PII-sensitive outputs for regulated customers (healthcare / finance) — require anonymization policies.
- Local dev-mode must not encourage drift vs production model; we should clearly label dev runtime as an approximation and include quantization caveats.

Open questions (for eng/product alignment):
- Sampling policy for fallback diff reports: random vs error-triggered vs time-windowed? (Input requested from applied-ml)
- SLA implications: if we expose per-route SLOs, do we offer financial remedies or only alerting? (legal + sales consult)
- Cost of storing paired-sample outputs for 30/90 days — upper bound estimate needed.

Operational asks for Customer Success (CS):
- Run a focused follow-up with the 6 customers who reported tail-latency issues to capture exact traffic shapes and SDK versions (owner: Ethan).
- Offer beta list for fallback-diff report to customers who run rollouts monthly (owner: Sofia).

Proposed prioritization (shortlist):
1) Queue-time header + console histograms (Quick -> High impact)
2) Route-level cost CSV (Quick -> Medium impact)
3) Fallback diff MVP (Medium effort -> High customer clarity)
4) Local dev-mode exploration (Longer, strategic for Private)

Next steps / meeting asks:
- Sync: eng-observability (lead), product-hosted-api, applied-ml, CS field reps — proposed 2027-10-14 to align scope.
- Create epics: CS-queue-tracing, CS-fallback-diff, CS-route-cost-export.
- Assign owners to quick-win tickets this week and publish an interim note to affected customers.

Appendix A — signal counts (rough):
- Tail-latency mentions: 18 unique customers, 27 threads.
- Fallback quality complaints: 9 customers, 12 rollout events.
- Cost attribution asks: 14 customers (mix of hosted and dedicated).

Appendix B — sample support snippet (redacted):
- "At 2027-09-05T14:23 our campaign had ~600qps for 3m, at 14:25 some sessions returned two truncated messages and we required an emergency rollback. Trace shows 99th went from 120ms -> 930ms" (redacted).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Ethan to collect SDK versions and replay shapes by 2027-10-08.
- Product to confirm sampling budget for diff reports before 2027-10-11.
- CS to draft customer-facing one-pager explaining measurement changes (queue headers) — include example curl/response.

-- end of working extract --

(Will convert to a cleaned initiative brief if devs/product prefer but keeping this raw for field signal traceability.)
